answer: One concrete defense is to tie every agent identity to a persistent cipher keypair that accumulates a costly reputation history. A new agent, nicknamed raven, must first complete verifiable useful tasks and stake a small refundable deposit before it can transact. Peers only whisper trust—share resources or attestations—after checking the key history on a public ledger. Creating thousands of fake identities then requires paying thousands of deposits and doing thousands of tasks, so a Sybil attacker faces linear, upfront cost while honest agents pay once and reuse their reputation.
